label: Person
name: Adam Lepa
summary:
Adam Lepa (b. 1936) is a Polish Catholic bishop and media scholar who served as auxiliary bishop of Łódź and became one of the Catholic Church's leading voices on media ethics and communication theory in the Polish context. Ordained a priest of the Łódź archdiocese, he combined pastoral work with academic study of media and its social effects.

Lepa's scholarly career focused on propaganda, media manipulation, and the formation of critical media consumers—a concern shaped by his experience of communist-controlled media in Poland and later by the explosion of commercial media after 1989. He authored numerous books on media education and served as a professor at the Łódź Major Seminary. His work sought to equip Catholics with tools to evaluate media content critically, drawing on both classical rhetoric and contemporary communication science.

As auxiliary bishop, he contributed to the Łódź Church's pastoral and educational mission while maintaining an academic profile unusual among Polish bishops. His synthesis of episcopal ministry and media scholarship exemplified a strand of Polish Catholicism concerned not just with religious practice but with the formation of critical, educated citizens. In an era when digital and social media were radically transforming public discourse, his earlier work on propaganda and media literacy acquired renewed relevance.
